name: Mriganka Sur
description: Mriganka Sur directs MIT's Simons Center for the Social Brain and is renowned for his rewired ferret experiments in the 1990s, in which he rerouted visual input into auditory cortex and demonstrated that the cortex self-organizes according to input statistics — a foundational result for cortical plasticity theory. His lab pioneered in-vivo two-photon imaging of cortical circuits across development and disease, revealing dendritic computation rules at single-synapse resolution. Sur's collaborative work on gamma oscillations — specifically 40 Hz sensory stimulation via light and sound — has been licensed to Cognito Therapeutics for clinical trials in Alzheimer's disease, targeting clearance of amyloid and tau via glymphatic entrainment. He received the Karl Spencer Lashley Award from the American Philosophical Society and has been elected to the National Academy of Sciences. His lab also has active programs modeling autism-spectrum circuit differences with genomically-edited primate models.
